claims.text: The nanoalloy contains Fe, Co, Cr, Ni, and Mn.
The initial FeCoCrNiMn nanoalloy has an FCC structure.
Structural stability at high temperature is governed by a stable surface oxide layer.
Chemical stability at high temperature is governed by a stable surface oxide layer.
The surface oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
The surface oxide layer acts as a barrier to degradation.
The stable oxide layer forms through reaction of the nanoalloy with oxygen.
Oxide-layer formation reduces the rate of subsequent oxidation.
The oxidation rate will be 30% lower than that of the untreated baseline.
Structural stability will improve by 25% relative to the untreated baseline.
Structural stability can be assessed from lattice-parameter change and oxide-layer thickness.
The proposed test uses in situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy from 500 to 1000°C at 10°C/min.
The primary experiment is conducted in a controlled argon atmosphere.
The stated baseline is the same high-entropy nanoalloy without surface modification or treatment.
The prediction is bounded to 500–1000°C and a heating rate of 10°C/min.
An oxidation-rate increase greater than 20% relative to baseline is designated as a falsifying outcome.
A structural-stability decrease greater than 15% relative to baseline is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The primary condition specifies a controlled argon atmosphere, while the mechanism requires reaction with oxygen; no oxygen partial pressure or residual-oxygen source is specified.

The intervention is characterization and heating rather than a surface modification, while the baseline is defined only as material without surface modification or treatment. Thus, the proposed test and baseline are not clearly distinct despite a claimed relative improvement.

The main prediction is posed under argon, but falsification is performed under oxygen instead. Changing the reactive atmosphere makes an oxidation-rate increase non-decisive for the prediction under argon.
